title: Brass batch chain: Morris et al. (2011) Chapter 4
description:
Two Morris control volumes in series. The first reproduces Example 4.2 (batch charge preparation for a brass melting furnace); the second takes its product as an initial charge, adds a declared zinc make-up, and balances to a final alloy. Everything here is non-reacting mixing, which is the only kind of boundary Chapter 4 can represent.

The Zielinski et al. (2019) process model is present as a third, standalone instance. It is deliberately NOT connected: COMPOSITION_AUDIT.md section 6.3 shows that none of its twenty equation outputs can legally enter a Morris control volume, because the model publishes no component identity and every one of its boundaries is reactive. It runs on its own terms, in evidence-replay mode, and its results are shown as what they are: a restatement of reported paper numbers, not a simulation.
source_ref: Morris, Geiger & Fine (2011), Introduction to Chemical Engineering, 4th ed., Chapter 4, Examples 4.2 and 4.5; Zielinski et al. (2019), Protein Expression and Purification 157, 63-69

defaults.notes: All masses are batch inventories in kg on a per-charge basis. No rate basis is used anywhere, because Chapter 4's steady-state mode requires one and no charge rate is known.

instances.label: Brass charge preparation
instances.notes: Three charges are mixed without reaction. D is determined by the copper balance, the zinc balance and sum(w) = 1 on C.

system.label: Batch charge preparation for a brass melting furnace
system.source_ref: Morris et al. 2011, sec. 4.5, Example 4.2, pp. 152-153

streams.label: copper charge
streams.note: The prose says 14000 kg but the flowsheet and the book's own 26600 kg total both require 14500 kg.

Cu.source_ref: Morris et al. 2011, Figure 4.11 and the 26600 kg total
Cu.note: The prose says 14000 kg but the flowsheet and the book's own 26600 kg total both require 14500 kg.

assumptions.statement: Each charge carries only the components it declares; anything omitted is listed in absent_components.
assumptions.rationale: Chapter 4 generates sum(w) = 1 over exactly the declared components, so an omission would silently read as a zero fraction.

instances.label: Alloying to specification
instances.notes: Takes D from brass_charge as its initial charge, adds a declared zinc make-up, and balances to the final alloy. Non-reacting: nothing here converts one substance into another.

system.label: Alloying of the mixed charge to specification
system.source_ref: Composition example built on Morris et al. 2011, Chapter 4

streams.label: alloy from the mixing step
streams.note: Supplied entirely by connection from brass_charge/out:D.

streams.label: zinc make-up charge
streams.note: A declared literal input, not a connection: 500 kg of zinc added to reach specification.

Zn.source_ref: declared on the composition graph (literal input brass_alloying/in:B:Zn)

assumptions.statement: 500 kg of pure zinc is added to the mixed charge.
assumptions.rationale: Declared on the composition graph, not derived. It is the only invented number in this control volume and is reported as assumed provenance so a reader can see exactly which result depends on it.

instances.label: Recombinant human insulin process
instances.notes: Runs on its own terms. It is not connected to either balance, and COMPOSITION_AUDIT.md section 6.3 explains why no connection is offered.

execution.notes: Evidence replay restates the paper's reported numbers and applies the accounting identities the paper supports. It is not a simulation, and the results panel labels it as such.

connections.label: mixed charge, kg
connections.notes: Both sides are MASS on a batch inventory basis; the units are identical so no conversion is performed.

brass_alloying/in:B:Zn.reason: The only invented number in this graph; declared, not derived.

notes: Load this file in Godot and press Run. Three instances execute in the order brass_charge -> brass_alloying -> zielinski_rhi.
